title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
gist: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2 as a three-model stack — a vision-language-action model that now controls full humanoids from feet to fingertips, an embodied-reasoning model (ER 2) acting as high-level planner and multi-robot coordinator, and an on-device VLA that adapts to a brand-new robot body in a few hours with under 200 examples. A single model checkpoint drives three different embodiments (Apptronik Apollo 2 with SharpaWave hands, Apollo 2 with Inspire hands, Franka Duo with Robotiq gripper), but DeepMind explicitly concedes multi-finger dexterity and movement speed still lag.

themes.theme: Whole-body control as the new capability frontier

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 extends robot foundation-model control from upper-body, table-top manipulation to full humanoid whole-body motion, including walking, crouching, stretching and balancing while manipulating objects.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Whole-body locomotion plus manipulation in one policy is the gating capability for humanoids leaving the demo table; watch whether rivals' VLAs still stop at the torso.
insights.quote: While our previous models controlled the humanoid’s upper-body to achieve table-top tasks, Gemini Robotics 2 expands physical AI into whole-body motions.
insights.locator: Humanoids in motion: Managing whole-body tasks

insights.claim: In DeepMind's demonstration, an Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoid given the single instruction 'put the watering can into the green bin in the bottom shelf' autonomously walks to a table, picks up the object, walks to shelves, and places it — one language command chaining locomotion and manipulation.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Apptronik is the named humanoid platform for Google's flagship robotics demo — a proxy read on which humanoid OEM has the deepest Google relationship.
insights.locator: For the first time, our model can now control entire humanoid robots

insights.claim: DeepMind openly concedes its humanoid robots are still too slow, stating movement speed needs to advance further before complex real-world whole-body tasks are practical.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Speed, not intelligence, may be the binding constraint on humanoid commercial ROI — discount deployment timelines built on capability demos alone.
insights.quote: While our robots have more to advance in movement speed, this is an important step towards the skills needed to complete more complex, real-world tasks that require whole-body coordination.
insights.locator: While our robots have more to advance in movement speed

insights.claim: A single Gemini Robotics 2 model checkpoint controls three physically different robots — the Apptronik Apollo 2 with SharpaWave hands, the same Apollo 2 with Inspire hands, and a Franka Duo with a Robotiq gripper — across whole-body and dexterous manipulation tasks.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: One checkpoint spanning multiple bodies means model economics amortize across the whole hardware ecosystem, favoring a horizontal 'robot intelligence layer' over vertically integrated single-robot stacks.
insights.locator: Gemini Robotics 2 controlling three different embodiments

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 adapts to entirely new bi-arm robot embodiments in a few hours of adaptation time, typically using fewer than 200 demonstration examples, even when the new body has drastically different shapes, sensors and degrees of freedom.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Sub-200-sample embodiment transfer collapses the data moat that robot-specific startups rely on; robot-data-collection businesses are the most exposed.
insights.quote: We can now adapt to new bi-arm robot embodiments with just a few hours of adaptation time, typically with less than 200 examples.
insights.locator: Adapting fast on-device models for any robot

insights.claim: The cheap cross-body adaptation in Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 comes from 'motion transfer' techniques inherited from the earlier Gemini Robotics 1.5 model, indicating a compounding technique lineage rather than a one-off result.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: The capability is cumulative across releases, so each Gemini Robotics generation widens the transfer gap rather than resetting it.
insights.locator: This model is natively multi-embodiment and inherits

insights.claim: DeepMind frames the core industry bottleneck as robots being pre-programmed or teleoperated for narrow repetitive sequences, unable to learn independently or transfer skills between robot bodies — positioning transferable learning, not hardware, as the scarce input.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: If the scarce asset is the intelligence layer, hardware margins compress toward commodity while model licensing captures value.
insights.quote: Most robots are pre-programmed or teleoperated for narrow, repetitive task sequences.
insights.locator: Most robots are pre-programmed or teleoperated

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2 can drive a five-fingered, 22 degree-of-freedom SharpaWave hand on the Apollo 2 robot to perform delicate actions such as tying knots and sealing a ziplock bag.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: 22-DOF control of deformable objects like knots and ziplocks is a concrete capability marker to benchmark competing dexterous-hand suppliers against.
insights.locator: The model can now control the five-fingered, 22 degree-of-freedom

insights.claim: DeepMind reports that while Gemini Robotics 2 achieves medium-to-high success on whole-body and two-fingered gripper tasks, multi-finger dexterous manipulation remains the weakest category and is still challenging.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Near-term commercial robot deployments will skew to gripper-based tasks; humanoid-hand-dependent business cases remain speculative.
insights.quote: While Gemini Robotics 2 achieves a medium to high success rate for whole-body and gripper-based dexterous tasks, the multi-finger dexterous manipulation remains challenging.
insights.locator: Each bar represents the average success rate

insights.claim: The same Gemini Robotics 2 model handles both anthropomorphic multi-fingered hands and standard two-fingered parallel grippers (on a Franka Duo doing tight-packing tasks), meaning end-effector choice becomes an application decision rather than a model-architecture commitment.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Existing industrial gripper fleets can inherit foundation-model intelligence without retooling to humanoid hands — a faster, cheaper adoption path than humanoids.
insights.locator: It can also operate standard two-fingered parallel grippers

insights.claim: DeepMind states it has not yet reached human-level dexterity and is still working to advance precision and speed toward that bar.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Explicit self-assessed gap to human parity is a useful calibration against vendor claims of imminent general-purpose labor replacement.
insights.quote: We are continuing to advance the level of precision and speed to achieve human-level dexterity.
insights.locator: We are continuing to advance the level of precision

insights.claim: DeepMind splits robot intelligence into a two-tier architecture: Gemini Robotics ER 2, a vision-language model acting as the high-level brain that plans, communicates with humans and tracks progress, and a separate vision-language-action model that executes motor control.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: The reasoning/action split mirrors the orchestrator-plus-executor pattern in software agents and suggests where third parties can plug in — the ER layer is the API surface being commercialized first.
insights.locator: Unlocking advanced tasks with agentic reasoning and multi-robot collaboration

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics ER 2 enables robots to execute task sequences lasting several minutes and involving hundreds of decisions, while self-correcting when an individual step fails.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Multi-minute, hundreds-of-decisions horizons with recovery is the threshold where robots can replace whole workflows rather than single motions — track horizon length as the key scaling metric.
insights.locator: In this update, we are enabling robots to more reliably execute

insights.claim: DeepMind is introducing multi-robot collaboration in which different types of robots communicate and work together on workflows a single robot could not complete alone.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous robot fleets coordinated by one model shifts the buying unit from individual robots to fleet orchestration software — a recurring-revenue layer above hardware.
insights.locator: Furthermore, we are introducing multi-robot collaboration

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics ER 2 adds temporal grounding — understanding when tasks begin and end and pinpointing the moment key events occur — which DeepMind calls a step change in progress understanding.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Event-level progress tracking is the prerequisite for unsupervised long-horizon autonomy and for auditable robot work logs in enterprise settings.
insights.locator: Gemini Robotics ER 2 now understands when tasks begin and end

themes.theme: Safety as a benchmark and standards play

insights.claim: DeepMind is introducing ASIMOV-Agentic, a new benchmark for agentic safety orchestration that measures whether an embodied reasoning agent can refuse unsafe tool calls issued by the vision-language-action model beneath it.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Owning the safety benchmark is a standards-setting move; whoever defines the eval shapes future regulatory and procurement criteria for embodied AI.
insights.locator: We’re introducing ASIMOV-Agentic, a new benchmark

insights.claim: ASIMOV-Agentic also scores whether the robot agent can predict that a task is impossible and proactively request human intervention when uncertain, making calibrated uncertainty an explicit product requirement rather than a research nicety.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Escalation-on-uncertainty implies human-in-the-loop staffing persists in early deployments, capping near-term labor-cost savings.
insights.locator: It also measures the agent’s ability to predict whether a task is possible

insights.claim: DeepMind claims Gemini Robotics ER 2 is its safest robotics model to date on safety-constraint-following and human-proximity benchmarks, able to detect nearby humans, trigger safety tool calls and bring the robot to a safe stop — which it ties directly to collaborative safety standards compliance.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Framing model capability against collaborative-robot safety standards is the on-ramp to factory and warehouse sales where certification, not demos, gates purchase orders.
insights.quote: This is a key requirement in collaborative safety standards.
insights.locator: Additionally, with enhanced embodied reasoning

insights.claim: DeepMind is releasing its robotics stack in tiers: the reasoning model Gemini Robotics ER 2 is generally available on Google AI Studio and in private preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, while the action models (VLA and On-Device) remain restricted to early-access partners.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Reasoning is being commoditized to developers while motor control stays gated — the control layer is where Google intends to retain leverage and pricing power.
insights.locator: Gemini Robotics ER 2, our reasoning model, is now available

insights.claim: DeepMind names Apptronik, Boston Dynamics and Agile Robots as robotics partners on the Gemini Robotics 2 effort, and demonstrates the on-device model on Dexmate, SO101 and Trossen platforms.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: A concrete map of hardware firms aligned to Google's robot brain — useful for screening private-market exposure and for anticipating who is locked out.
insights.locator: Finally, we’d like to thank our partners

insights.claim: DeepMind emphasizes that Gemini Robotics 2's intelligence can run locally on-device because many robotic applications must operate without network latency or internet connectivity.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: On-robot inference shifts value toward edge silicon and away from per-call cloud API revenue for the physical-AI segment.
insights.quote: Many robotic applications need to operate without network latency or internet connectivity.
insights.locator: Adapting fast on-device models for any robot

insights.claim: DeepMind explicitly positions Gemini Robotics 2 as a milestone toward 'solving AGI in the physical world,' arguing that unlocking robotics requires moving past single-task automation to general-purpose intelligence.
insights.speaker: Carolina Parada
insights.so_what: Google is folding robotics into its AGI narrative, signaling sustained capex and strategic patience rather than a discretionary side project.
insights.quote: Gemini Robotics 2 marks an important milestone on the path toward solving AGI in the physical world.
insights.locator: Building towards general-purpose physical AI
